answers.answer: For each held office card, roll one die simultaneously, add one per fatigue on that card, and add one more for the Chairman. A modified result of 1–2 does nothing; 3–4 adds fatigue; 5+ retires the officeholder. A retiree moves to Pensioners, the card is flipped into Vacant Offices, and its fatigue is returned to the supply. Commanders have no office card and do not make normal office attrition rolls.

Only players who retired at least one pensioner may select or discard a London Season display card. They act in descending order of their actual total retirement spending; ties go to the player with the most total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from the PM. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. A selected or discarded card is not replaced during selection; if the display empties, every remaining eligible player is skipped. At the end, discard all cards left in the display and refill exactly three cards—prestige faceup and blackmail facedown—even if nobody took a card. Return all unused Pensioners to their supplies.

At the start of a player's Family phase action, check where their opportunity marker was at phase start. They choose a main family action once, or twice if the marker already matched that action, and then place or move the marker onto the chosen action. After that main action, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action; it is never doubled by the marker and does not move the marker. With four vacant offices and the marker already on Enlist Writer, the doubled action can place two writers, and the four-vacancy rule adds one additional writer once this turn, for three writers total.
answers.evidence: Family phase procedure; Enlist Writer row

answers.answer: After all family actions, while both Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court as a Company share and lower Debt by one; repeat while both remain. If Debt is gone, slide all remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. The money paid when seeking a share goes to the bank; it is not paid into Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: New Company shares; Seek Share row

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending order of the number on the backs of their cards. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that family member into the office; the member's owner receives the office card. For an ordinary office hire involving the hirer's own family, verbal consent is required from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool. When promoting an officeholder, transfer its fatigue to the new card and insert the old card, now vacant, into the ascending hiring order. If there is no candidate or the designated hirer is vacant, skip the office; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

The former Chairman first announces how many shares constitute a pure majority, meaning more than half of the current shares. Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner's Company shares into the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. If nobody gets the required support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. The Chairman piece remains a Company share for dividends, majority calculations, and scoring, but it cannot be traded or invested in a firm.

Before a Company-office success check, commit its resources and any cash; all cash for that check comes from the acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice and subtract penalties, then roll and use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that office's actions, returns its officeholder to the supply, discards its fatigue, and flips its card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander and firm procedures can modify this. Do not take an action with no effect or chance of success, such as trading without a ship or deploying without dice merely to trigger possible officer losses.

The Chairman may take up to three Debt advances freely, adding £5 to Balance for each, but may never advance past the Debt track end. Each additional advance beyond three requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting the Chairman. The Chairman must then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, lowering Balance by each transfer. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved, subject to the borrowing limits; cash already in office treasuries stays there for those offices to use.

Shipping must spend its treasury until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the owner's consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China if that office exists. Extra ships remain only until Refresh.

For Trade, declare regions including the Presidency's home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 in the President's treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. A failure may be retried during that President's uninterrupted opportunity if affordable; at most one successful Trade per President per turn, and catastrophe removes the President. On success, fill one order per ship in its sea zone, as many as possible within the declared regions. Place the first actual writer at the home port; each next order must be adjacent to one already filled by this Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A President cannot fill another Presidency's home region, even if that other office is vacant. Increase Balance by each order's printed value, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it that turn under deregulation. The President receives £1 from the bank per order, and owners receive £1 per writer placed. Use dividers to separate adjacent writers from different Presidencies for Refresh.

A Commander may target their own Presidency's home region, any region associated with it, or any region bordering an associated region. They cannot target another Presidency's home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company region is a legal target only if it has unrest or a closed order that the action can affect. Exhausted officers and regiments each provide one die; local alliances provide their printed number of dice, and their strength can be used only once that turn for Deploy or defense and cannot be split. Subtract the target's strength plus all other regions in its empire, counting the target once; Company-controlled defense strength is zero. After every attempt, each owner rolls one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll officer-loss dice.

After a successful Deploy, take loot equal to £4 per target tower plus its faceup loot modifier, with a minimum equal to the surviving participating officers in this attempt plus one. Distribute each payout cycle in order: £1 for the Commander and £1 for each of their used surviving officers; then £1 per used surviving officer for other families clockwise; then £1 per used regiment and per used local-alliance piece to the bank. Repeat the whole cycle from the Commander until all loot is distributed or the cash runs out. The Commander also takes one trophy per target tower. Then remove the target's tower and dome, and all matching empire flags if it was a capital; open all its orders and remove all its unrest. If it was not already Company-controlled, put its loot/control token region-side up above the associated President's box and put the Governor overlay on the conquered region, sending only the office card to Vacant Offices for later hiring. Do not create Governors/overlays if Governor General is in play. If the Elephant was in the conquered region and faced outward, move it fully inside. On catastrophic failure, return half the Commander's family's trophies rounded up and return the Commander member to supply; exhausted officers still check losses, and the Commander has no office card to vacate.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy; Successful control procedure; catastrophe rule

answers.answer: The Governor takes the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces that pool by one regardless of the result. On success, take £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, and choose exactly one benefit: Build, Commission a regiment, or Tax. Build takes two successful Build actions: first put a partially built Company ship in the Governor's region if none is there, then on a later successful Build complete it into the sea zone associated with that Governor's President. Commission puts a regiment in that President's Army. Tax adds an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President's treasury; every Tax after the first this turn adds unrest in the region. Any unsuccessful roll adds one unrest there; catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal rule. Continue with the shrinking dice pool until choosing to stop, no dice remain, or catastrophe occurs.

Company expenses reduce Balance by £1 per existing Debt, each officer or regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones including China; Commanders are excluded. If Balance cannot cover expenses, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one per loan until the Debt track ends, and continue taking emergency loans even at maximum Debt. Newly added emergency Debt does not add an expense this turn. After using emergency loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance to expectations for current Standing; if below expectations, lower Standing one. After that, the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends, costing one cash per Company share per dividend and paying £1 per share to each owner including the Chairman. If total dividend cash paid is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one. Reaching the leftmost Standing space causes Company failure.

An Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region also triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve the primary attack first, then secondary regions in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order; within each Presidency, its Commander orders the attacks. A normal primary Crisis attack strength is its ordinary Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in its target. For a primary Foreign Invasion, use only the ordinary attack die, without added unrest. Each secondary Rebellion's strength is only the unrest cubes in that region, with no event modifier or empire strength. The associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces totaling the attack strength, or as much as possible; local alliances use printed strength and cannot be split. If the newly exhausted defense strength is insufficient, perform Region Loss. If sufficient, remove all unrest in the attacked region and give the Commander one trophy; if this successful defense defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one tower from the attacking region if possible. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts in their stead, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that player chooses defense pieces and gets or loses no trophies. A successful primary Invasion against the Company also applies empire growth.

After voting, support of −1 or less fails: discard the law, resolve a dilemma's If Failed text, return the Opposition Leader's token and give them the PM dial. The new PM moves the proposed policy one space in either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. Support of zero or more passes: place the law with passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy, then resolve immediate law effects. In either outcome, finally restore every voting card to its regular orientation. If a law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.

In 1758 and Long 1710, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call the special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. It uses the ordinary voting procedure and support threshold, with the listed exceptions: there is no policy accompanying the law; a failed vote does not remove the PM or discard the Deregulation law, and the PM may vote against it. On passage, lower Debt by one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. On failure, increase Company-share scoring value by flipping or placing the Court VP token, up to the maximum of ±3. The 1813 scenario starts deregulated.

To form a firm, a player who currently manages no firm returns one eligible Company share to supply or flips a workshop to its invested side, flips their family board, places a family member as the first firm share, sets the value cube to the track's leftmost space, and takes £5 from the bank into the firm's London treasury. To invest in an existing firm, get the manager's consent and contribute an eligible Company share or workshop; this creates one firm share and sends £5 from the bank to London. A firm may have at most ten shares; further investments still add £5 but create no share. The Chairman share cannot be used, and Company shares cannot be invested at all when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space. A share created this turn cannot be invested, even if traded away. Invested workshops never return to uninvested status, give no workshop bonus and no Company-failure VP, and remain invested even if the firm fails.

Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn. Managers simultaneously and secretly choose a trade zone/home port, requiring at least one ship, and secretly bid cash from London treasury; a closed home port is allowed when choosing. Alternatively, choose Hobnob: no bid, trade, or dividends, but still pay expenses and retain the previous dividend marker. Reveal bids simultaneously, while strategy cards stay facedown until their matching Presidency begins. At that Presidency's operations, before other actions, matching firms reveal strategy and roll one die per committed £1, paying the bid to the bank. At least one 1 or 2 allows trade. Firm initiative is ship count minus successful dice (1s/2s), possibly negative. The President's successful Trade produces initiative the same way. After that success, fill orders from lowest initiative upward; the President chooses order among ties, and the Company does not automatically go first. If the President is vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill after the Commander/Governors have had a chance, with Chairman choosing initiative ties. Each firm fills open orders up to ships plus one, starting from its home port and tracing its own connected filled route; it fills each particular order at most once. Firms may refill orders filled by others/the Company this turn, and the Company may refill a firm's orders. A previously filled order pays half its listed revenue, rounded down. Advance firm Value one space per full £6 added to India treasury this turn.

At the start of Revenue, before Company revenue, firms pay expenses in initiative order, with ties resolved by managers' most windows and then PM clockwise order. The firm pays £1 per charter ship plus the higher of its share count or firm value, using either or both treasuries. After expenses, dividends may be paid only from India treasury; each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager. With the manager's consent, a shareholder may forgo payment for any number of shares on any dividend. Record total actual cash paid out on the dividend marker. An active non-Hobnob firm paying nothing records zero; Hobnob keeps its previous marker. Sweep remaining India cash into London. If the firm cannot pay expenses, it dissolves unless rescued. Dissolution sends shares to Debtor's Prison at −1 VP each, returns ships to shipyards, returns the charter to the family side, and leaves workshops invested. Rescue can use emergency investments under normal Company-share/workshop rules (even if the ten-share cap prevents more shares): pay expenses, lose remaining cash, and lower Value one per emergency investment; alternatively merge with one other firm, which must first pay its own expenses if unpaid and cover the failing firm's unpaid expenses.
